text: Task commit subjects must place the em-dash DIRECTLY after the phase number: gate.mjs phaseOwnFiles greps the literal 'phase <N> —', so 'feat(scope): phase 1 task 1.1 — ...' matches NOTHING and every file in that commit is classified foreignCommitsInRange. The gate then derives testScope/reviewScope/specialist floors from an almost-empty phase-own set. Correct form: 'feat(scope): phase 1 — task 1.1: <what>'. Unrecoverable once sibling sessions have interleaved commits into the range, because the fix would be a rebase over their work.

The arc prompt classified 'measure --flow do-arc --assert 12500' as one of three ENVIRONMENTAL host failures. It is not: it is a repo-state standing red measuring 14917 tokens on any host, already dispositioned in plugins/zeroh-roadmap/DIET-LEDGER.md and assigned to the diet lane, and the gate has no known-failure mechanism to pass over it (green is arithmetic over slot exit codes; checkPhaseConsistency refuses a non-green done flip; PassingGateResultShape refuses passed!==total). The other two WERE real and were fixed in-seam: node_modules/.bin/tsx has a '#!/usr/bin/env node' shebang, so under a PATH-scrubbed test the exec SUCCEEDS and env exits 127 with "env: 'node': No such file or directory" — matching neither the ENOENT branch nor the 'not found' wording, so a fail-OPEN tsx-absent contract was classified as a blocking eval-error. Precedent for the ratchet is phase 1995: escalate, then a user ruling.

When a phase's notes leave a blast-radius ambiguity (widen the SHARED shape or only one use site?), read the step's own verify clause before escalating: a whole-file negative grep can only pass under one of the readings, so the planner already decided it mechanically. Phase 2 task 2.4's `! grep -qF "z.enum(['session', 'codex'])"` spans the file, which is only satisfiable by widening the shared DriverShape — the coherent choice anyway, since a record shape refusing an unknown lane would drop exactly the third-driver phases the arc exists to measure.

A gate slot that exceeds the harness's foreground command cap is not a reason to park or checkpoint: launch the gate run itself with run_in_background so the harness wakes you on exit, and spend the wait on the review round against the already-frozen diff. The plugin's own unit slot (node --test, concurrency 1, ~60 files) runs ~15-20 min against a 10-min Bash cap; splitting it by hand would improvise a scoping command the gate protocol forbids.

A guard's reach rule must be derived from the registry's own declared capabilities, not from what the fixture assumed: the phase-4 parity fixture encoded 'a claude driver cannot reach the codex model', which was false — codex exec is a headless child the plugin's own run lane already uses. The fix was to probe and DECLARE the capability, then re-pin the guard, never to keep the convenient assumption.

A delegated test-writer will hardcode values that a repo-wide ratchet owns (a model id, a path, an argv literal) because its brief names the behaviour, not the ratchets. Phase 9 task 9.4: test-engineer wrote 'gpt-5.6-sol' five times into a fixture and tripped drivers.test.mjs's one-home-for-model-ids scan — invisible to the task's own scoped suite, caught only by a mid-phase FULL run. Two takeaways: name the live ratchets in the delegation brief, and run one full suite mid-phase rather than saving it all for the gate.

A fix round is where the second bug lives: rounds 1, 2 and 3 each found real defects in the PREVIOUS round's fixes — twice a fix had recreated the exact symptom it closed (an archive gate that skipped the already-gone lane; a guard added to one of two, then two of three, call sites). When a review round is a fix round, point the next reviewer AT THE FIX COMMIT and name what each fix was supposed to close, not just at the phase diff.

Before claiming a helper is a shared rail, grep for EVERY call site — twice in phase 6 a guard was added where the reviewer had pointed and missed a third caller (disposeWorktree had three: phase land, arc land, and archiveReviewLane, the last firing from a READ command). Count the call sites first, then fix all of them in one edit.

A gate agent (quality-pass) committed its own fixes with subject 'fix(phase-10): …' — the curate foreign-detector requires the binding 'phase N —' grammar and refused the whole squash range as foreign. Either pass the commit grammar into gate-agent prompts or have the orchestrator own the commit.

fixture-consumer harness runCli dropped ALL stderr on exit-0 runs: execFileSync exposes stderr only on the thrown error object, so success-path advisory lines were silently unobservable and any doesNotMatch(stderr) assertion passed vacuously. Swapped to spawnSync (captures both streams always). Check this when a wired test asserts stderr on a passing command.
PhaseTaskShape requires done:false on every authored task (no schema default) — forgotten on three consecutive plan-phase authorings (10, 11, 13); write it into the task template at authoring time.

A guard-mutation drive done with a string replace can silently hit the WRONG occurrence: mutating "lane === 'plan' && state === 'complete'" in codex.mjs patched nextStepHint (line 751) instead of the statusCodex re-entry key (line 853), and the mutated run came back GREEN — indistinguishable from a vacuous test. A green mutation drive is a claim about the MUTATION as much as about the test: assert the anchor is unique (or patch by line and echo the mutated line back) before believing the result.

A fixture test that drives an admission-gated verb inherits the box's AMBIENT capacity: `arc next` returns action 'blocked' exit 2 once executors busy >= maxExecutors, so test/fixture-consumer/arc-next.test.mjs N1/N4 red on a busy host with nothing wrong in the diff (reproduced at 5 busy vs limit 3 while four sibling codex lanes ran; the same fixture passes by hand at 2 busy). PROVEN remedy, and the trap inside it: pinning ZEROH_ROADMAP_CAPACITY_PROBES alone does NOTHING under a gate slot, because capbuild runs a sanitized systemd unit that STRIPS the variable — the pin only lands with CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV="ZEROH_ROADMAP_CAPACITY_PROBES" (26/26 green pinned, 24/26 unpinned, same tree). Two rules: a gate slot's green silently encodes who else was running, so re-run a RED unit slot serially before reading it as a defect; and an env-seam pin that must survive capbuild has to be declared in CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV or it is a no-op that looks like a refuted hypothesis.

integrationRefOf reads mergePolicy.autonomousPushRefs[0] (cli/lib/config.mjs), so the LAND TARGET and PUSH AUTHORIZATION are the same field: a consumer that wants `phase land` to work at all must name its integration branch there, and naming it silently authorizes autonomous push to it. There is no way to say 'land here, push nowhere' short of leaving the field unset and losing landing entirely (the fallback is a literal 'develop'). Split the two: an explicit integrationRef key for the target, autonomousPushRefs for the authorization. Surfaced when declaring the ref to unblock landing also enabled a push to a real GitHub origin — and the operator had concluded no origin existed from a `git remote -v | head -2` that truncated it away, which is its own lesson: never conclude absence from a truncated listing.
